notes: CalibForge again leads, but this is the one task of my five where the other pools contribute real signal. CalibForge supplies a whole family of 'write the program that this supplied simulator will run, within a line/step budget' tasks — one of them (software-engineering_20260601_053159_004) even uses /app/sim and a line cap — plus the bitwise-only arithmetic task, which is the gate-construction skill in pure form. TMax contributes two genuinely good items its retrieval had buried (task_000405_db54ffe9, a dataflow-circuit evaluator, and task_000258_60a61045, hand-assembling bytecode); neither was in the top of the shortlist, both came from my own searches. Terminal-Lego is the only corpus with the two mathematical halves as standalone tasks — isqrt (task_09170), Fibonacci (task_09187, task_09194) — and those are strongly verified, so it beats the v1 pool here on content the old pool simply lacked. Recursive-Task-Synthesis's ARM64 assembly cluster is a fair analogue (algorithms with registers and branches only) but is entirely `absent`-graded; I could not find a graded RTS equivalent. SWE-Smith reduces to cantools bit-field arithmetic and SWE-Rebench to quantum-circuit libraries — the latter is a surprisingly apt domain match for gate composition, but as issue-shaped bug fixes they lose on task_form and should stay out of the top 10.
